postTitle: Income Replacement Ratio: How Much Income You Need in Retirement
topic: What the 70 to 80% retirement rule assumes, and where an assumption fails

assumptions.notes: Lesson: the 70 to 80% figure rests on retirement saving stopping (10 to 15% of gross pay), work costs stopping (5 to 10%) and tax falling (5 to 10%): roughly 20 to 30% removed. Real households can sit 20 points either side: some live on 40 to 50%, others need 100% or more.

caption.instagram:
The rule says retirement needs 70 to 80% of your pay. What does that number assume?

Three things dropping away when work stops. Saving for retirement itself, often 10 to 15% of pay before tax. Work costs such as commuting, another 5 to 10%. And tax, which often falls with a lower income, 5 to 10% more. Together that is roughly 20 to 30% of pay gone without any change in how someone lives.

Each assumption can be wrong for a given household. Someone who saved little privately, already works from home, or will be taxed on retirement income much as on wages has less to drop. Real households sit well either side: some live on 40 to 50% of their old income, others need 100% or more. The figure comes mainly from US planning studies; the lesson builds the number line by line from actual spending.
